songInfo.title: More Than Words
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: G - A - B - C - D - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Played using G major shapes in half-step down tuning (sounding concert Gb major) across the main G - Cadd9 - Am7 - C - D loop

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D# - E
scalesUsed.application: Supplies the soulful B7 (V/vi) secondary dominant chord that pulls into Em during the chorus ('Then you wouldn't have to say')

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Intimate, percussive acoustic Ionian warmth enriched with 9th/7th chord extensions and classic secondary-dominant (B7 to Em, D7/F# to G) voice leading
keyAndScale.keySignature: 1 sharp (G major shapes in Eb tuning, sounding as concert Gb major)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: Nuno Bettencourt's masterclass in solo acoustic accompaniment: a shimmering G to Cadd9 to Am7 to C-D loop locked to a hypnotic percussive slap on beats 2 and 4.
mainProgression.description: Nuno Bettencourt's masterclass in solo acoustic accompaniment: a shimmering G to Cadd9 to Am7 to C-D loop locked to a hypnotic percussive slap on beats 2 and 4.

sectionProgressions.description: Fingerstyle pluck-and-slap groove keeping the 3rd-fret high G note ringing across G and Cadd9

sectionProgressions.section: Bridge / Turnaround ('What would you do if my heart was torn in two?')
sectionProgressions.progression: Em - Am7 - D7 - G - B7 - Em
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: vi - ii7 - V7 - I - III7 - vi
sectionProgressions.description: Circle-of-fifths motion and a poignant B7 secondary dominant resolving into E minor

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus Resolution ('More than words is all you have to do')
sectionProgressions.progression: Am7 - D7 - G - G7 - C - Cm - G
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: ii7 - V7 - I - V7/IV - IV - iv - I
sectionProgressions.description: Features the gorgeous minor-plagal C major to C minor (IV to iv) cadence before resolving home to G
G major chord-tone arpeggio and percussive slap coordination drill

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Warm acoustic tonic with pinky anchored on the high G (1st string 3rd fret)
Cadd9 (IVadd9) - Lush subdominant sharing the top two 3rd-fret notes (D and G) with the G chord
Am7 (ii7) - Gentle supertonic chord preparing the V chord turnaround
D / D7 (V) - Dominant chord resolving back to G
B7 (III7 / V of vi) - Secondary dominant creating aching tension before landing on Em
Cm (iv) - Borrowed minor subdominant providing the heart-melting 'More than words' cadence

techniques.name: Percussive Fingerstyle Acoustic Slap & Chord-Tone Plucking
techniques.description: Nuno Bettencourt's signature acoustic groove where the thumb and fingers pluck bass notes and upper triads while slapping the low strings against the frets on beats 2 and 4 like a snare drum

notes: Am7: X-0-2-0-1-3 (with pinky on high G, then lifting to open E)
sequence: Pluck the root bass note with your thumb on beat 1, followed by an upward brush/pluck of the treble strings on the '&' of 1
On beat 2, drop your right-hand thumb and palm onto the low strings so they click percussively against the fretwire
Immediately pluck the chord tones on the '&' of beat 2 and 'a' of beat 3 before slapping again on beat 4
Keep your ring and pinky fingers anchored on fret 3 of the B and high E strings when shifting from G to Cadd9
tips: The percussive slap comes from rotating your forearm slightly so the side of your thumb strikes the 6th/5th strings over the soundhole—don't hit the wooden top too hard
Practice the right-hand groove on a single G chord until the beat 2 and 4 snare-slap becomes completely automatic
Tune down a half step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb) if you want to play along directly with the original recording

sections.name: Intro & Verse Fingerstyle Groove
sections.description: Nuno Bettencourt's iconic G - Cadd9 - Am7 - C - D fingerstyle pattern with backbeat string slaps.
notes: Keep frets 3 on strings 1 and 2 anchored through G and Cadd9
Land a crisp thumb slap on beats 2 and 4 of every bar
Split the fourth bar between C major (2 beats) and D major (2 beats)

sections.name: Bridge & Minor Plagal Cadence
sections.technique: Secondary Dominant & Borrowed Minor Voice Leading
sections.description: The emotional bridge moving through B7 to Em and resolving via the classic C to Cm minor-plagal cadence.
sections.progression: G - B7 - Em - C - Cm - G
notes: Let the B7 chord (X-2-1-2-0-2) pull soulfully into Em
Bring out the chromatic move from E natural (in C major) to Eb (in C minor) before resolving to D (in G major)
Keep the percussive backbeat steady underneath the richer harmonies

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Arpeggio and upper-string voice-leading exercise tracing the high G → E → F# melody notes over the main progression.
notes: Pluck bass notes with your thumb (p) and treble strings with index (i), middle (m), and ring (a)
Listen to the top-string melody: 3rd fret (G) → open (E) → 2nd fret (F#)
Keep your right hand relaxed and close to the strings

guitar.recommended: Washburn EA20 / Festival Series Acoustic or Martin D-28 (tuned down 1/2 step to Eb)
guitar.pickup: Small-diaphragm condenser microphones in stereo XY pair + subtle piezo blend

settings.bass: 5 (controlled low end so thumb slaps don't boom)

effects.other: Light studio compression to balance the percussive thumb slaps with fingerpicked notes

beginner.title: Chord Shapes & Soft Strumming
steps: Master G (3-2-0-0-3-3) to Cadd9 (X-3-2-0-3-3) keeping your ring and pinky fingers anchored
Learn Am7, C, and D and play the four-bar verse cycle with a gentle down-up strum
Add the bridge chords (Em, B7, and Cm barre chord or Cm6 triad)
Play through the chord chart smoothly at 92 BPM

intermediate.title: Percussive Thumb Slap on Beats 2 and 4
steps: Practice the Pluck (beat 1) → Slap (beat 2) → Syncopated Pluck ('&' of 2) → Slap (beat 4) groove on a stationary G chord
Carry the percussive slap smoothly through the G - Cadd9 - Am7 - C - D loop
Include the high-G pinky melody lift on Am7 (3rd fret to open E)

advanced.title: Full Nuno Bettencourt Studio Embellishments
steps: Execute the D7/F# thumb-wrapped bass walkups and rapid grace-note hammer-ons
Nail the staccato stops and passionate strumming climax in the final chorus
Sing the lead or harmony vocal line while maintaining the syncopated slap groove

commonMistakes: Lifting all fingers when moving from G to Cadd9 instead of keeping frets 3 on strings 1 and 2 anchored
Pausing the percussive slap on beats 2 and 4 when changing chords
Slapping with the flat palm (which sounds thuddy) instead of letting the thumb bounce low strings off the frets
practiceRoutine: 4 minutes: Right-hand Pluck-Slap-Pluck-Slap groove isolation on a single G chord at 75 BPM
4 minutes: G → Cadd9 → Am7 → C → D loop with unbroken 2-and-4 backbeat slaps
4 minutes: Bridge transitions (B7 → Em and C → Cm → G)
4 minutes: Full song playthrough at 92 BPM
focusAreas: Consistent snare-like thumb slap on beats 2 and 4
Syncopated '&-of-2' chord pluck immediately after the beat-2 slap
Smooth C major to C minor barre transition
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 75 BPM and line up your thumb slaps directly on clicks 2 and 4
Increase in 5 BPM increments up to 92 BPM
Practice transitioning from the fingerstyle groove into the strummed bridge sections without rushing
